# Cale AI Workbench 0.24.15 for Windows

The Browser address bar and Ask Cale field now display readable text, placeholders and a visible caret in both themes. The tab strip, page reading panel and task status follow the selected theme.

Use **Read page** to extract visible text from the current tab. **Copy text** copies the extraction, and **Use in Chat** opens it as a draft. Large pages show a notice when the page reader reaches its limit.

**Ask Cale** automatically uses an installed local abliterated model with tool support. It prefers Qwen3.5 abliterated 9B when it fits the task, then the 2B variant, and checks memory, context length and tool support before dispatch. The 9B Browser assistant is available in Settings → Local AI. This update changes automatic Browser model selection.

## Verification

On the desktop build, typed text measured 14.34:1 contrast in the dark theme and 15.40:1 in sage. Placeholders exceeded 6.6:1 in both themes. The embedded browser extracted the visible text of a local test website. A clipboard test sink received the exact text.

The installed 9B abliterated model filled two randomized fields, submitted the owned form once and verified the result against the page. The local web server independently confirmed the submitted values. This test covered a top-level form. Website-specific behavior, including controls inside cross-origin frames, varies.

Forty-three targeted native tests and ten Chromium page-script checks passed. One opt-in local inference fixture in the native unit suite was skipped.
The verified form task used four model calls and 4729 reported tokens. Stop acknowledged an in-flight action in 26 ms. Manual input cancelled a separate pending inference before it could submit.
Source commit e4cacfbef8ba59b5e1b7bafeb060ab87aa0d94b0.
